title: Break The Spin · Nov 15-16
subtitle: 6 posts, all real photos: R,S tonight; T,U,O,P Nov 16.

posts.theme: Buttigieg jokes about FAA ground stop
posts.quote: BUTTIGIEG JOKED HE'D HELP REBOOK FLIGHTS FROM THE HOTEL BAR. THE LAST NATIONWIDE GROUND STOP HAPPENED ON HIS WATCH.
posts.alt: Two panels: official portrait photos of former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg on the left and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy on the right. Bold text below reads: Buttigieg joked he'd help rebook flights from the hotel bar. The last nationwide ground stop happened on his watch.
posts.caption:
Pete Buttigieg has jokes about the FAA ground stop.

Speaking to reporters in Denver at a Democratic conference, the former Transportation Secretary quipped, "I will be available in the hotel bar following the concert for anybody who needs to rebook their flights." He added, "It is not clear to me why that redundancy did not prevent an outage of this magnitude." He said he had no inside information about the cause and was watching it as a traveler with a flight of his own.

Fair question. Here is another one. In January 2023, with Buttigieg running the Department of Transportation, an FAA system outage halted domestic departures nationwide. He ordered a review and promised fixes. The aging air traffic control system he oversaw for four years is the same one that went dark this week.

The FAA lifted the latest ground stop after more than four hours, but nearly 7,000 flights were delayed or canceled.
posts.first:
Officials say this outage was not a cyberattack. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin pointed to aging infrastructure that needs updating, President Trump told Fox News the system broke down because of its age, and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy says the investigation into whether a contractor or equipment failed is still under way.

That is the real story. Air traffic control has been running on outdated technology for years under presidents of both parties. Buttigieg had four years and billions in infrastructure money to modernize it.

Cracking jokes from the sidelines is easy. Explaining why the problem was still there when he left is harder.

posts.theme: Van Hollen: path to oust Schumer
posts.quote: VAN HOLLEN SAYS HE HAS A PATH TO OUST SCHUMER. THE DEMOCRATS' CIVIL WAR JUST WENT PUBLIC.
posts.alt: Two panels: official portrait photos of Sen. Chris Van Hollen on the left and Sen. Chuck Schumer on the right. Bold text below reads: Van Hollen says he has a path to oust Schumer. The Democrats' civil war just went public.
posts.caption:
The fight for control of Senate Democrats is now out in the open. Schumer has led Senate Democrats since 2017.

Sen. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland went on CNN's State of the Union and said he can take the top job from Chuck Schumer. "I have a path to get there, no doubt about it," he said. "There's a hunger for change within the Senate Democratic Caucus."

Schumer's team answered by releasing a list of senators it says are voting for him. Van Hollen claims some of the names on that list have privately committed to him instead. The leadership vote is set for December 1, and Schumer's camp is reportedly trying to move it up.

Van Hollen's loudest backer is Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed, who said Van Hollen earned it by flying to El Salvador to check on Kilmar Abrego Garcia.
posts.first:
Think about what this fight is really about. Democrats just won the Senate, and instead of a victory lap, their caucus is split over whether the party moves even further left.

Schumer is no moderate. But the faction pushing Van Hollen sees him as too cautious, and the new class of senators arriving in January is making that case loudly.

If Van Hollen wins, the most liberal voices in the caucus will be setting the agenda. Whoever wins on December 1 will set the tone for the next two years in Washington. Republicans should be watching closely, because the winner will tell you exactly which Democratic Party they will be facing.

posts.theme: Rubio: stop quoting laws to men with swords
posts.quote: MARCO RUBIO TO THE GLOBALISTS: "STOP QUOTING LAWS TO MEN WITH SWORDS."
posts.alt: Official portrait photo of Secretary of State Marco Rubio. Bold text below reads: Marco Rubio to the globalists: "Stop quoting laws to men with swords."
posts.caption:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio did not mince words about the International Criminal Court.

In a keynote to a room full of conservative lawyers and judges at the Federalist Society's National Lawyers Convention in Washington, Rubio ripped the court for claiming the power to investigate, prosecute and jail American citizens without America's consent. He said it has made itself "judge and jury and executioner of the international order."

Then came the line that drew laughs from the room: "Stop quoting laws to men with swords." He joked that it was not exactly politically correct.

Rubio argued that international law has become a weapon for a global elite, used to attack American decisions like strikes on cartel boats in the Caribbean and the capture of Nicolas Maduro. He aimed the same scorn at the United Nations, warning Americans not to submit "to the sterile vision of radical judges or soulless global bureaucrats."
posts.first:
The quote comes from an old story about the Roman general Pompey, told when he brushed off legal objections from a city he was taking. Rubio's point is simple: rules mean nothing to people who will not follow them, and America should not hand its sovereignty to courts that answer to nobody here.

The United States never joined the ICC, and Congress never agreed to put Americans under its jurisdiction.

You can believe in law and order and still refuse to let foreign bureaucrats decide who gets prosecuted in America. That is the line Rubio just drew, out loud.

posts.theme: NYC DSA votes to push AOC for president
posts.quote: NYC SOCIALISTS VOTED 291-123 TO PUSH AOC FOR PRESIDENT. THEIR CITY COUNCIL PLAN? FLAGGED AS 100% AI-WRITTEN.
posts.alt: Two panels: official portrait photo of Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez on the left and a photo of New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani on the right. Bold text below reads: NYC socialists voted 291-123 to push AOC for president. Their City Council plan? Flagged as 100% AI-written.
posts.caption:
New York City's socialists have their 2028 candidate picked out.

The NYC chapter of the Democratic Socialists of America voted 291 to 123 at its annual convention to urge Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez to run for president in 2028. Co-chair Gustavo Gordillo called it "a commitment to encouraging and building the foundation for a presidential campaign," though not a formal endorsement. He added, "AOC and New York City DSA are committed to building a stronger democratic socialist movement."

The same convention laid out plans to take over the New York City Council in 2029. There is just one problem. According to Politico, an AI-detection tool called Pangram rated the City Council resolution 100% AI-generated. Two other resolutions were flagged too, one on expanding DSA membership on community boards and one on outreach to South Asian communities.

The chapter's co-chair pushed back: "We are highly skeptical of the results coming out of Pangram."
posts.first:
This is the same movement that elected Zohran Mamdani mayor, and now it wants AOC in the White House. Whatever you think of them, they are organized, they are winning local races, and they are thinking a full presidential cycle ahead.

AOC has represented the Bronx and Queens in Congress since 2019 and has not said whether she will run. The vote was not even close. But the people who built her base just told her they are ready.

And if the plan to run America's biggest city council really was written by a chatbot, maybe voters should ask who will be doing the governing.

posts.theme: Mace: There is no Arab America
posts.quote: REP. NANCY MACE: "THERE IS NO ARAB AMERICA, ONLY THE UNITED STATES. ONE COUNTRY, ONE FLAG, ONE NATION. AMERICA FIRST"
posts.alt: Photo of Rep. Nancy Mace, posted on her official account in 2025. Bold text below quotes her: There is no Arab America, only the United States. One country, one flag, one nation. America First.
posts.caption:
Rep. Nancy Mace just put it in one sentence.

"There is no Arab America, only the United States. One country, one flag, one nation. America First," the South Carolina Republican wrote on X.

It is not a new position for her at all. Last spring she blasted South Carolina's Arab American Heritage Month proclamation as "exactly the kind of pandering that has defined Columbia for too long," asking, "How does this proclamation lower the cost of groceries?" Her answer: "It doesn't."

She has made the same case on citizenship, backing an amendment on officeholders with dual citizenship with one line: "one country, one allegiance, or you do not serve."

The point is not where anyone's family came from. Millions of Americans trace their roots to the Arab world, and they are every bit as American as anyone else. The point is that once you are here, you are an American first.
posts.first:
This used to be the mainstream view in both parties. Immigrants came, learned English, raised the flag and became Americans. Hyphens were for heritage, not for loyalty. Assimilation was never about erasing anyone. It was about joining something bigger.

Now a statement like Mace's gets called divisive. But a country that celebrates every separate identity and never the shared one eventually stops being one country at all.

You can honor where your grandparents came from and still put the United States first. Most Americans of every background already do. Mace is just saying out loud what they live every day.

posts.theme: Reich wants SpaceX seized; SpaceX catches ship
posts.quote: A FORMER CLINTON CABINET SECRETARY WANTS DEMOCRATS TO SEIZE SPACEX. SPACEX JUST CAUGHT A SPACESHIP RETURNING FROM ORBIT.
posts.alt: Photo of a SpaceX Starship booster descending toward its launch tower, with a red-ringed circle inset of former Labor Secretary Robert Reich. Bold text below reads: A former Clinton cabinet secretary wants Democrats to seize SpaceX. SpaceX just caught a spaceship returning from orbit.
posts.caption:
Robert Reich wants the government to take SpaceX. SpaceX just did something no government has ever done.

The former Clinton Labor Secretary said on his podcast last month that Democrats should be "laying the groundwork for nationalizing Starlink and SpaceX." His reasoning: "It should be a public corporation. We should not ever have that kind of power in one person's hands."

Musk fired back on X: "Stealing companies is a serious crime. Prison for Reich."

Then SpaceX answered with a rocket. On its 15th Starship flight, the company caught the Starship spacecraft itself with the launch tower's mechanical arms after more than 22 hours in orbit and 26 Starlink satellites deployed. It is the first time the ship has ever been caught. The booster was lost over the Gulf, a reminder that testing is hard.
posts.first:
You may have seen posts claiming Democrats are preparing to freeze all of Musk's assets and strip his citizenship. We could not find any plan like that. What is real is what Reich said, and that is bad enough. He also claimed 75 percent of Musk's wealth depends on taxpayers and offered no evidence for it.

Private companies took bigger risks, moved faster and did it with private investment. That is how America catches rockets out of the sky. Starship is the rocket NASA is counting on to return Americans to the Moon, and SpaceX still has to prove it can do it again.

Break the spin. The real quote is alarming enough without the exaggeration, and the real achievement is impressive enough without the hype.
